newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Thomson BankWatch rates Russia's Menatep B.
newsitem.headline: Thomson BankWatch rates Russia's Menatep B.

text.p: New York-based bank rating agency Thomson BankWatch said on Tuesday it had given Bank Menatep, one of Russia's biggest banks, a high non-investment "B" rating.
"Bank Menatep is arguable Russia's most important investment bank," BankWatch president Ramin Habibi said in a report.

The bank falls under the "B" ceiling the agency allocated Russia in October because of uncertainty surrounding President Boris Yeltsin's health, the unstable political climate, budgetary pressures and failures to comply with International Monetary Fund economic targets.
"Our ratings reflect liquidity and earnings concerns," Habibi said.
BankWatch said Menatep was the seventh biggest Russian bank by assets, and had become an important channel of state support to the textile industry and other subsidised economic sectors.
It gave Menatep a short-term local currency rating of LC-2, the second highest of its four grades for this category.
BankWatch also rated the largest bank in Russia's Far East, Dalnyvostochny Bank, "B" and "LC-3".
Both banks benefit from their accreditation to the World Bank/Europan Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) Financial Institutions Development Project, the report said.
